content_blocks.text: Command-Line Application Architecture matters because Dart programs need predictable behavior, explicit contracts, and examples that can be verified. This topic focuses on structuring CLI applications, input handling, and separation of concerns. Keep the lesson’s core distinction separate from runtime, SDK, package, or platform details that may vary. When you build on this idea, state your assumptions, try the smallest useful example, and check edge cases before integrating it into a larger project.

Common mistakes: confusing a language guarantee with a runtime or package behavior; skipping malformed/empty inputs; relying on undocumented version assumptions; and changing multiple things before reproducing a failure. Prefer explicit naming, a small test, and official documentation.
